title_en: Comic Book 'Journey to the West 24: The Small Thunder Temple'
source_file: 连环画《西游记24：小雷音寺》（6-10岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 西游记
之二十四
小雷音寺
小雷音寺
《西游记》之二十四
原著 吴承恩
改编
绘画
河北美术出版社

[P2] 内容提要
这本连环画是根据古典神话小说《西游记》第六十五——六十六回编绘的。描述唐僧师徒去西天取经，一个妖怪在半路上假扮如来佛，设立小雷音寺，引诱唐僧入内。唐僧只看表面，不辨真假，不听孙悟空的劝告，结果落进妖怪圈套，悟空也被妖怪的金铙合住。后来二十八宿救出悟空，妖怪又用“乾坤袋”把二十八宿等神将捉去，只有悟空逃出。经过一番争斗，最后在弥勒佛的帮助下，降伏了妖怪，唐僧师徒才继续向西天赶路。

1 唐僧师徒离了祭赛国，一路西行，经过不少难关，越过不少山川。这天，正行时，忽然看见一座高山，山中金光闪闪，彩云纷纷，从楼台殿阁里，传来钟鼓的声音。

徒弟们，看那是什么地方？

[P3] 2 悟空看罢，觉得那座寺院有些凶气，劝唐僧不要进去，免遭暗害。
3 唐僧催马加鞭，来到寺院门前，见“雷音寺”三个大字，慌得滚下马来，跪在地上便拜，口里还不住地骂悟空，说悟空哄了他。悟空说：“师父，门上是四个字，为何只念三个字？”

[P4] 就是小雷音寺，
也必有佛祖在内，
我弟子心诚，远来
拜佛，如何怪你？
4 唐僧爬起来再看，乃“小雷音寺”四个字。唐僧仍
要进去。悟空拦住道：“不能进去，此处凶多吉少，若有祸
患，你莫怪我。”
5 这时，只听山门里有人叫：“唐僧，你自东土来拜见
我佛，怎么这样慢慢腾腾？”唐僧听后，急忙下拜，八戒、沙
僧也跪倒磕头，只有悟空留在后边。

[P5] 6 走到二层门内，看见如来大殿。殿门外摆列着五百罗汉及无数菩萨、圣僧、道者。唐僧与八戒、沙僧一步一拜，悟空不但不拜，还左右看个不停。
7 这时，又听得莲台座上厉声高叫：“孙悟空，见了如来为何不拜？”悟空这时已看出是假佛、假寺，便双手抡棒，上前边打边骂：“这伙妖孽，十分大胆，怎么假借佛名，败坏如来清德，休走，看棒！”

[P6] 8 只听得半空中叮当一声，撇下一副金铙，把悟空连头带足，合在金铙之内。
9 唐僧、八戒、沙僧也被捆绑起来。原来装佛祖的是妖王，其余都是些小怪。他们现出妖身，将唐僧、八戒、沙僧抬入后边准备蒸熟吃掉。

[P7] 10 悟空合在金铙里，左拱右撞，抡棒乱打，不能出来。挣不破，钻不出，急得满身是汗。
11 夜晚，等妖魔们都睡熟之后，悟空便念个诀咒，唤来了五方揭谛、六丁六甲等神前来帮忙。但是任凭众神怎样使力，这金铙就如长就的一般，一点也拉不开。

[P8] 12 于是，揭谛又去天宫，请来了二十八宿等天兵天将。
13 天兵天将为了不惊动妖魔，便悄悄地拿出兵器，掀的掀，撬的撬。弄到三更，金铙还是纹丝不动。

[P9] 14 天将亢金龙用了千斤之力将自己的角钻进铙内。
15 悟空将金箍棒变成一个钢钻儿，叫亢金龙忍住疼，他在角上钻了一个小孔。

[P10] 16 悟空把身子缩小，钻进小孔去了。
17 亢金龙不知费了多少力气，才将角拔出，悟空这才被带了出来。

[P11] 18 悟空拿出铁棒，照着金铙用力打去，当的一声，如同崩倒铜山，把金铙打成碎块。
19 大小群妖被惊醒，在妖王带领下，出来叫战，这时，悟空与众菩萨早已跳到九霄云外。

[P12] 20 悟空听到妖王叫战，便带领众菩萨和天兵天将按落云头，与妖王打将起来。
21 战了五十回合，不见输赢。众菩萨和天兵天将，便吆喝一声，把妖王围在中间。

[P13] 22 正在这时，只见妖王从腰间解下一条旧白布搭包，往上一抛，只听一声响亮，把悟空和众神将一起装进白布搭包里去了。
23 妖王叫小妖们取了三五十条绳子，捉一个，捆一个，抬到后边。

[P14] 徒弟，快来救我，往后的事，凭你处置，我再不言了。
24 半夜时分，悟空听到唐僧哭泣说：‘徒儿呀，我后悔没听你的话，才遭此魔难。’悟空听了也很难过，便使了个遁身法，将身一缩，脱下绳子，走到唐僧跟前。
25 悟空解了唐僧，放了八戒、沙僧和众神将，又牵过马来，叫他们快些出去。

[P15] 26 出门后，才知没带出行李。悟空叫他们下了山坡，去平地等候，然后自己回来寻找。
27 悟空好不容易找到行李，不管担绳偏正，挑上肩，往楼下就走。谁知这时脱了一头，扑的一声，将行李落在楼板上。

[P16] 28 这一声，惊醒了众妖。妖王前前后后找不见唐僧等，便取了武器，率领众小妖赶了出来。
29 正当八戒、沙僧、众神将与妖魔混战时，悟空也赶来参战。

[P17] 30 妖王打个哨子，叫群妖留心，然后解下搭包，撒将下来，悟空看得清楚，便叫道：‘不好了！快走啊！’顾不得八戒、沙僧等，一个跟斗，跳到九霄云外。
31 悟空落在东山顶上，咬牙切齿痛恨妖怪，独自一个，坐着出神。他忽然想起武当山有个荡魔天尊，也许他有办法救出师父，便驾筋斗云飞向武当山。

[P18] 32 悟空会见了荡魔天尊，说明来意。荡魔天尊即派龟蛇二将和五大神龙帮助悟空降伏妖魔，去救唐僧。
33 那妖王正坐在宝阁寻思悟空借兵之事，忽听小妖来报：‘孙悟空和几个龙蛇龟相，在门外叫战！’

[P19] 34 妖王披挂好出来迎战。五条神龙，翻云吐雨，龟蛇二将播土扬沙，各执刀枪剑戟，与妖王争斗起来，悟空抡铁棒在后助战。
35 战了半个时辰，那妖王又解搭包在手，悟空见了心惊，叫道：‘大家要小心！’果见那妖王把搭包撒出，悟空顾不得五龙、二将，驾起筋斗云，逃了出去。

[P20] 36 悟空在云端上，眼看着妖王把五条龙神和龟蛇二将一搭包装去了。
37 悟空落下云头，斜靠在山巅石上，没精打采，合着眼睛，思索对策。

[P21] 38 猛听得有人呼唤，睁眼一看，原来是日值功曹，悟空便要找他出气。
你这毛神，一向在那方贪图血食，不本份！今日却来搅打两棒，老！
39 原来日值功曹是前来报信的，说唐僧师徒和众神将性命危险，叫悟空赶快去泗洲大圣国师王菩萨那里求援。
国下有四大圣手名四天大，他，有程仗个，他，还有个四洲有，而这个王言个大，你可找你有小张和，住

[P22] 40 悟空果然请了小张太子和四大将到小雷音寺来骂战。
41 小张太子见妖王出来，挺枪便刺，四大将一拥而上，
悟空使棒劈头就打。妖王抡着他那条狼牙棒，左遮右架。

[P23] 42 交战多时，不分胜负。见妖王要解搭包，悟空忙叫太子小心。
43 妖王把搭包一撒，四大将与太子，便被装进搭包，只有悟空脱逃而去。

[P24] 44 悟空立在西山坡上心想：当初师父要听自己的话，也不会有此祸。如今，东求西告去借救兵，仍不能救他们出来，这如何是好？
45 正在这时，忽见西南天上一朵彩云落地，悟空手搭凉篷观看，原来是弥勒佛。
我此来，专为这小雷音寺的妖怪。
来来佛祖，你慢去！

[P25] 46 原来这妖怪就是弥勒佛管磬的黄眉童子，他趁弥勒外出，把几件宝贝盗走，假佛成精。那搭包就是弥勒佛的“乾坤袋”，那条狼牙棒是个敲磬的槌儿。
47 弥勒佛与悟空商量好收妖的办法后，嘱咐悟空，与妖怪交战时，只许败，不许胜，诱他到这山坡下来。
你往西去，见妖怪当面放手，他就跟来。

[P26] 你变不使搭包，再
有三五个，也打不过
老孙！
你计穷力尽，这次
还逃得命吗？
48 悟空来到小雷音寺山门外叫战，那妖王穿戴整齐，
带了宝贝，走出门来。
49 妖怪为了要与悟空比个上下，便答应不使宝贝。悟
空双手抡棒，劈头打了下来。

[P27] 50 悟空且战且退，把妖怪引下山坡。
51 二人打得正起劲时，悟空虚晃一招，败阵就走。那妖赶到西山坡下，悟空忽而不见了，只见一片瓜田。

[P28] 52 那妖怪战得口干，正想弄口水喝，再去找悟空。于是就向看管瓜田的老头要一个又熟又甜的西瓜来解渴。
53 那老头把西瓜捧给妖怪，妖怪接过来，张口便啃。

[P29] 54 原来这瓜正是悟空变的。悟空进了妖怪肚里，不管好歹，翻跟斗，竖蜻蜓，大弄手脚，妖怪疼得死去活来。
55 这时，看管瓜田的老头也现出弥勒本相。妖怪抬头一看，见是主人公，慌忙跪倒在地，双手揉着肚子磕头求饶。

[P30] 56 弥勒佛上前，一把揪住，解了搭包，夺下敲磬的槌子，才叫悟空出来。悟空为了这妖怪，东奔西走，实在恼恨，于是左一拳，右一脚，又打了一阵，才从妖怪口中跳出。
57 悟空现了本相，拿起铁棒又要打那妖怪，弥勒却将妖怪装进袋里去了。

[P31] 58 悟空领着弥勒佛来到小雷音寺。那些小妖得知老妖被擒，各自四散逃命。
59 弥勒佛把打碎的金铙合成一副，别了悟空，驾云回去了。

[P32] 60 悟空解下唐僧、八戒、沙僧等，并找出行李马匹。
61 悟空又和八戒打开地窖，把众神将救出。唐僧披上袈裟，拜送他们。

[P33] 62 唐僧师徒送走众神后，整理好行李，又奔西天去了。
欲知后事，请看下册《七绝山》。

full_text_en:
[P1] Journey to the West
Chapter Twenty-Four
Little Temple of the Sound of Thunder
Little Temple of the Sound of Thunder
Chapter Twenty-Four of "Journey to the West"
Original work by Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by
Illustrated by
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

[P2] Content Summary
This illustrated storybook is adapted from chapters 65-66 of the classical mythological novel "Journey to the West." It describes how Tang Sanzang and his disciples journeyed westward to obtain scriptures. A demon disguised as Buddha established the Little Thunder Sound Temple to lure Tang Sanzang inside. Tang Sanzang, seeing only the surface, failed to distinguish truth from falsehood and ignored Sun Wukong's warnings, falling into the demon's trap. Wukong was also trapped by the demon's golden casket. Later, the Twenty-Eight Mansions rescued Wukong, but the demon then used the "Qiankun Bag" to capture the Twenty-Eight Mansions and other celestial generals, with only Wukong escaping. After a fierce battle, and with the help of Maitreya Buddha, the demon was subdued, and Tang Sanzang and his disciples continued their journey westward.

1 Tang Sanzang and his disciples left the Jisai Kingdom, traveling westward, overcoming many difficulties and crossing numerous mountains and rivers. That day, as they walked, they suddenly saw a tall mountain, with golden light shimmering and colorful clouds swirling. From the pavilions and halls, the sound of bells and drums could be heard.

Disciples, look—what place is that?

[P3] 2 After looking around, Wukong felt that the temple had a sinister aura and advised Tang Sanzang not to enter, to avoid being ambushed.
3 Tang Sanzang urged his horse forward and arrived at the temple gate. Seeing the three large characters “Lei Yin Si” (Temple of Thunderous Sound), he panicked, fell off his horse, knelt down and began to worship, while muttering angrily at Wukong, saying Wukong had deceived him. Wukong said: “Master, there are four characters on the gate, why are you only念ing three?”

[P4] It's the Little Thunder Sound Temple,
there must be the Buddha inside,
my disciples are sincere, having come far
to worship the Buddha, how could you blame me?
4 Tang Sanzang got up and looked again, seeing the four characters "Little Thunder Sound Temple". Tang Sanzang still
wanted to enter. Wukong blocked him, saying: "You can't go in, this place has more danger than safety. If there's trouble,
don't blame me."
5 At this moment, someone inside the mountain gate called out: "Tang Sanzang, you've come from the Eastern Land to worship
me, the Buddha, why are you moving so slowly?" Tang Sanzang, upon hearing this, hurriedly bowed down, and Bajie and Sha
Seng also knelt and磕ed their heads, while only Wukong remained behind.

[P5] 6 They entered the second gate and saw the Great Hall of Buddha. Outside the hall stood five hundred Arhats and countless Bodhisattvas, holy monks, and sages. Tang Sanzang, Zhu Bajie, and Sha Wujing bowed step by step, but Wukong not only refused to bow, but kept looking around.
7 At this moment, a loud voice boomed from the lotus throne: “Wukong, why don’t you bow to Buddha?” Wukong had already realized this was a fake Buddha and a fake temple. He swung his staff with both hands, rushing forward while shouting and striking: “You evil fiends, how dare you impersonate Buddha and defile the purity of Buddha? Don’t run—here comes the staff!”

[P6] 8 A clanging sound came from the sky, and a golden casket was dropped down, trapping Wukong head to toe inside.
9 Tang僧, Bajie, and Sha僧 were also tied up. The one pretending to be the Buddha was the demon king, and the rest were minor monsters. They revealed their true forms and carried Tang僧, Bajie, and Sha僧 to the back to be steamed and eaten.

[P7] 10 Wukong was trapped inside the golden casket, thrashing left and right, wildly swinging his staff, unable to get out. He couldn't break free, couldn't dig out, and was so anxious that he was drenched in sweat.
11 At night, after the demons had all fallen asleep, Wukong recited a spell and summoned the Five Directions' Guardians, the Six Ding and Six Jia deities, and others to help. But no matter how hard the gods strained, the golden casket was as if grown together, and they couldn't pull it open at all.

[P8] 12 Then, the Jieti went to Heaven again and summoned the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions and other heavenly soldiers and generals.
13 The heavenly soldiers and generals, to avoid alarming the demon, quietly took out their weapons, some trying to lift it, others to pry it open. By the third watch, the golden censer remained completely immovable.

[P9] 14 The heavenly general Kang Jinlong used immense force to drive his horn into the golden censer.
15 Wukong transformed his golden cudgel into a steel drill, told Kang Jinlong to endure the pain, and drilled a small hole in the horn.

[P10] 16 Wukong shrunk his body and crawled into the small hole.
17 Kangjinlong, after expending great effort, finally pulled his horn out, and Wukong was thus pulled out.

[P11] 18 Wukong pulled out his iron staff, struck the golden censer with all his might. With a loud clang, like a copper mountain collapsing, he smashed the censer into pieces.
19 The small and large demons were awakened, and under the demon king's lead, came out to challenge. At that moment, Wukong and the Bodhisattvas had already jumped to the ninth heaven.

[P12] 20 Wukong heard the demon king challenge, and led the Bodhisattvas and heavenly soldiers to descend from the clouds, engaging the demon king in battle.
21 After fifty rounds of fighting, neither side had won. The Bodhisattvas and heavenly soldiers shouted together, surrounding the demon king in the middle.

[P13] 22 At this moment, the demon king took off an old white cloth sack from his waist, threw it up, and with a loud sound, he stuffed Wukong and the heavenly generals into the white cloth sack.
23 The demon king ordered the little demons to fetch thirty to fifty ropes, catch one, tie one, and carry them to the back.

[P14] Disciple, come quickly and save me. From now on, do as you please, I won't say another word.
24 In the middle of the night, Wukong heard Tang Sanzang crying: 'My disciple, I regret not listening to you, and thus we've fallen into this disaster.' Wukong felt deeply saddened and used his shrinking technique, shrunk his body, removed the ropes, and walked to Tang Sanzang.
25 Wukong untied Tang Sanzang, freed Bajie, Sha Wujing, and the heavenly generals, then brought over the horse, urging them to leave quickly.

[P15] 26 After leaving, they realized they had forgotten to take their luggage. Wukong told them to go down the slope and wait on flat ground, while he returned to look for it.
27 Wukong finally found the luggage. Without caring whether the shoulder strap was crooked, he hoisted it onto his shoulder and started walking downstairs. But just then, one end slipped, and with a thud, the luggage fell onto the floor.

[P16] 28 This sound woke up the demons. The demon king searched everywhere for Tang Sanzang and others, then took his weapon and led the small demons out to chase them.
29 Just as Bajie, Sha Wujing, and the heavenly generals were engaged in a fierce battle with the demons, Wukong also arrived to join the fight.

[P17] 30 The demon king whistled, warning his minions to be alert, then untied the cloth sack and threw it down. Wukong saw clearly and shouted, 'It's bad! Run quickly!' Without regard for Bajie, Sha僧, and others, he flipped a somersault and leaped to the ninth heaven.
31 Wukong landed on the eastern mountain peak, grinding his teeth in hatred of the demons, sitting alone, lost in thought. He suddenly remembered that on Wudang Mountain there was a Demon-Slaying Heavenly Sovereign, who might have a way to rescue his master. So he mounted his somersault cloud and flew toward Wudang Mountain.

[P18] 32 Wukong met the Lord of荡魔 and explained his purpose. The Lord of荡魔 immediately sent the Turtle and Snake Generals and the Five Divine Dragons to help Wukong subdue the demons and rescue Tang Sanzang.
33 The demon king was sitting in his treasure hall, pondering Wukong's request for reinforcements, when suddenly a minor demon reported: 'Sun Wukong and several dragon, snake, and turtle generals are challenging us outside the gate!'

[P19] 34 The demon king, fully armored, came out to fight. Five divine dragons, swirling clouds and spitting rain, and the turtle and snake generals, stirring up dust and sand, each wielding swords, spears, halberds, and lances, fought against the demon king, while Wukong swung his iron staff to assist from behind.
35 After half an hour of battle, the demon king took out the cloth sack again. Wukong, seeing this, was alarmed and shouted, 'Everyone, be careful!' Indeed, he saw the demon king throw out the sack. Wukong, unable to care for the five dragons and two generals, mounted his somersault cloud and fled.

[P20] 36 Wukong was on the clouds, watching as the demon king packed the five dragon gods and the turtle and snake generals into a bundle and carried them away.
37 Wukong descended from the clouds, leaning slumped against a rock on the mountain peak, listless, eyes closed, pondering a strategy.

[P21] 38 Suddenly he heard someone calling. He opened his eyes and saw it was the Daily Duty Official. Wukong was about to vent his anger on him.
You foolish spirit! You've always been greedy for blood and flesh, acting unrighteously! Today you come to stir up trouble with two sticks, old man!
39 It turned out the Daily Duty Official had come to deliver a message: Tang Monk, his disciples, and the divine generals were in mortal danger. He urged Wukong to quickly go to the Great Sage Guoshi Wang Bodhisattva in Sizhou for help.
Under the realm, there are four great saints, named the Four Heavenly Greats. He, with his staff, one, he, and also this Four Realms have, while this King speaks of the great, you may find you have Xiao Zhang and, live

[P22] 40 Wukong indeed invited Xiao Zhang Taizi and the Four Great Generals to Xia Leiyin Temple to challenge the demon king to battle.
41 When Xiao Zhang Taizi saw the demon king emerge, he thrust his spear forward. The Four Great Generals rushed in together, and Wukong swung his staff down at the demon king's head. The demon king brandished his wolf-toothed staff, blocking and parrying from left and right.

[P23] 42 After fighting for a long time, neither side gained the upper hand. Seeing the demon king about to open his magic bag, Wukong hurriedly called out, 'Prince, be careful!'
43 The demon king threw open his magic bag, and the Four Generals and the Prince were immediately sucked in. Only Wukong managed to escape.

[P24] 44 Wukong stood on the western hillside, thinking: If only my master had listened to me at first, this disaster wouldn't have happened. Now, after seeking help everywhere, I still can't rescue them. What should I do?
45 At that moment, a colorful cloud descended from the southwest sky. Wukong shaded his eyes to look and saw it was Maitreya Buddha.
I have come specifically to deal with the demon of the Little Thunderous Temple.
Come, Master Buddha, please wait a moment!

[P25] 46 The monster was originally Huangmei, the boy who managed the bell for Maitreya Buddha. He stole several treasures while Maitreya was away and transformed into a fake Buddha. That bag was Maitreya's 'Qiankun Bag', and the wolf-toothed staff was a mallet used to strike the bell.
47 After Maitreya Buddha and Wukong discussed a plan to capture the monster, he instructed Wukong: when fighting the monster, you must only lose, never win, and lure him down to this slope.
Go west, and when you see the monster, let go right in front of him—he will follow.

[P26] You won't use the bag, even if there are three or five more, you can't beat me, Old Sun!
You're out of tricks and exhausted, can you escape this time?
48 Wukong came to challenge outside the gate of the Little Thunder Monastery. The demon king, dressed neatly and carrying his treasure, stepped out.
49 The demon, wanting to compare strength with Wukong, agreed not to use his treasure. Wukong swung his staff with both hands and struck down.

[P27] 50 Wukong fought while retreating, luring the demon down the slope.
51 As the two fought fiercely, Wukong feinted a move and pretended to retreat. The demon chased him to the foot of the western slope, but Wukong suddenly vanished, leaving only a field of melons.

[P28] 52 The demon, exhausted from fighting, was thirsty and wanted to get some water before going to find Wukong. So he asked the old man who tended the melon field for a ripe and sweet watermelon to quench his thirst.
53 The old man handed the watermelon to the demon, who took it and bit into it immediately.

[P29] 54 The watermelon was actually transformed by Wukong. Wukong entered the monster's stomach, and without caring for anything, he did somersaults, stood on his head, and made a big fuss, causing the monster to suffer terribly.
55 At this moment, the old man who was watching the melon field also revealed his true form as Maitreya. The monster looked up and, seeing the master, hurriedly fell to the ground, rubbing his stomach and bowing his head to beg for mercy.

[P30] 56 Maitreya stepped forward, grabbed the demon, untied the bag, took the mallet used for striking the bell, and then called for Wukong to come out. Wukong, having run around for this demon, was truly furious, so he punched and kicked left and right, beating him for a while before jumping out of the demon's mouth.
57 Wukong revealed his true form, picked up his iron staff, and was about to strike the demon again, but Maitreya put the demon into a bag.

[P31] 58 Wukong led Mile Fo to the Little Thunder Sound Temple. The little demons, upon learning that the old demon had been captured, scattered and fled for their lives.
59 Mile Fo repaired the shattered golden censer into a complete set, bid farewell to Wukong, and flew back on the clouds.

[P32] 60 Wukong freed Tang Sanzang, Baijie, Sha Wujing, and others, and retrieved their luggage and horse.
61 Wukong and Baijie opened the cellar and rescued the divine generals. Tang Sanzang put on his robe and bowed to send them off.

[P33] 62 After sending off the gods, Tang Monk and his disciples packed their belongings and set off again for the West.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《西游记》之二十四《小雷音寺》的封面页，展示了孙悟空挥棒击敌的插画，并列出了原著作者吴承恩、改编者、绘画者及出版社信息。
[P2] 本页为绘本《小雷音寺》的内容提要和第一幅画面，提要概述了唐僧师徒在小雷音寺遇险并最终脱困的故事情节；画面描绘了师徒四人行至高山，看到金光闪闪的楼台殿阁，孙悟空询问同伴那是什么地方。
[P3] 本页描绘了孙悟空察觉小雷音寺有凶气并劝阻唐僧进入，但唐僧不听劝告，执意前往，在寺门前见到“雷音寺”三字后激动下马跪拜，孙悟空则指出门上实为四个字，暗示其被蒙骗。
[P4] 唐僧在孙悟空的劝阻下仍执意进入小雷音寺，寺内有人呼唤他拜见佛祖，唐僧与八戒、沙僧跪拜，唯独孙悟空留在后方未拜。
[P5] 唐僧师徒进入小雷音寺二层门内，见殿外摆满罗汉、菩萨等，唐僧与八戒、沙僧跪拜，孙悟空则不拜并四处观察。随后，假佛在莲台座上质问孙悟空为何不拜，孙悟空识破其为妖孽，怒而挥棒上前攻击。
[P6] 孙悟空被金铙困住，唐僧、八戒、沙僧被妖怪捆绑，妖王现出原形，准备将他们蒸熟吃掉。
[P7] 本页描绘了孙悟空被困在金铙中挣扎不得，以及夜晚他召唤众神前来帮忙，但金铙纹丝不动，众人无法将其打开的情景。
[P8] 孙悟空被困在金铙中，揭谛前往天宫请来二十八宿等天兵天将前来营救，众人悄悄用兵器试图撬动金铙，但至三更时分仍无法打开。
[P9] 孙悟空被困在金铙中，天将亢金龙用角钻入铙内，孙悟空将金箍棒变成钢钻，在亢金龙的角上钻孔，试图破开金铙。
[P10] 孙悟空在亢金龙的帮助下，通过缩小身体钻入金铙钻出的小孔，最终被从金铙中救出。
[P11] 孙悟空用金箍棒击碎金铙，妖怪们被惊醒出来迎战，但孙悟空与众菩萨已趁机逃至九霄云外。
[P12] 孙悟空带领众菩萨和天兵天将与妖王交战，五十回合不分胜负，随后众人合力将妖王围在中间。
[P13] 妖王用白布搭包将孙悟空和众神将一并装入，随后命令小妖们用绳子将他们捆住并抬走。
[P14] 孙悟空在半夜听到唐僧后悔哭泣，便用法术脱身，解救了唐僧、八戒、沙僧和众神将，并牵马让他们尽快离开。
[P15] 孙悟空出门后发现未带行李，让同伴在平地等候，自己返回寻找；找到行李后挑着下楼，却不慎让一端脱手，行李掉落楼板。
[P16] 妖王被惊醒后率众小妖追击，八戒、沙僧与众神将与妖魔混战，孙悟空随后赶来参战。
[P17] 妖王解开搭包，孙悟空发现后立即逃脱，跳到九霄云外；随后他落在东山顶上，痛恨妖怪，并决定前往武当山求助荡魔天尊。
[P18] 孙悟空向荡魔天尊求助，天尊派龟蛇二将和五大神龙助其降妖救唐僧；与此同时，妖王正在思考孙悟空借兵之事，突然得知孙悟空与援军已在门外叫战。
[P19] 妖王与孙悟空及援军展开激战，五条神龙和龟蛇二将助战；战斗中妖王再次拿出搭包，孙悟空察觉危险后立即驾云逃脱。
[P20] 孙悟空在云端目睹妖王用搭包将五条龙神和龟蛇二将一并装走，随后他落地，靠在山巅石上，神情沮丧地思索对策。
[P21] 孙悟空在山巅遇见日值功曹，起初想发泄怒气，后得知唐僧师徒和众神将有生命危险，被劝去泗洲大圣国师王菩萨处求援。
[P22] 孙悟空请来小张太子和四大将，在小雷音寺外与妖王展开激战。小张太子挺枪刺向妖王，四大将和孙悟空也一同进攻，妖王则挥舞狼牙棒抵挡。
[P23] 孙悟空与小张太子及四大将与妖王激战，妖王欲用搭包收人，悟空及时提醒，但四大将与太子仍被装入搭包，悟空独自逃脱。
[P24] 孙悟空在西山坡上因无法救出师父而感到沮丧，此时弥勒佛驾云而来，表示专为降服小雷音寺的妖怪而来，孙悟空急忙上前迎接。
[P25] 弥勒佛向孙悟空揭示妖怪的真实身份，并告知其法宝来源；随后，弥勒佛吩咐孙悟空在与妖怪交战时假装战败，引诱妖怪到山坡下，以便实施收服计划。
[P26] 孙悟空在小雷音寺山门外挑战妖王，妖王穿戴整齐并携带法宝应战；为公平比试，妖王答应不使用法宝，孙悟空随即挥棒猛击。
[P27] 孙悟空与妖怪交战，边打边退，将妖怪引至山坡下；妖怪追至西山坡时，孙悟空佯装败退消失，只留下一片瓜田。
[P28] 妖怪在与孙悟空激战后口渴，向看瓜田的老头要西瓜解渴，老头递上西瓜，妖怪接过后立即大口啃食。
[P29] 孙悟空变成西瓜被妖怪吞下，在其腹中翻腾使其痛苦不堪；随后看瓜老头现出弥勒佛真身，妖怪见状跪地求饶。
[P30] 弥勒佛制服妖怪，救出孙悟空，并将其装入袋中。
[P31] 孙悟空带领弥勒佛来到小雷音寺，小妖们得知妖王被擒后四散逃命；弥勒佛将打碎的金铙修复后，与孙悟空告别，驾云返回。
[P32] 孙悟空解救了被擒的唐僧、八戒、沙僧及行李马匹，并与八戒一同打开地窖救出被囚禁的众神将，唐僧披上袈裟为他们送行。
[P33] 唐僧师徒送走众神后，整理行李继续西行；页面下方附有《西游记》连环画的完整目录，当前故事为第24册《小雷音寺》，下册为《七绝山》。
[P34] 本页为《小雷音寺》连环画的版权页，列出了原著作者、改编者、绘者、出版发行信息、ISBN、定价及印刷批次等出版信息。
